For supported proof-found clause-list runs, `--proof-object=1` now emits the C `SZS output start/end CNFRefutation` framing with represented mixed clause/formula ancestors before the proof root, uses represented proof-state clause and formula extraction-root stacks for proof-success root selection with a returned-clause fallback, appends represented processed/unprocessed `--full-deriv` roots when requested, emits C-shaped PCL/TSTP derivation or source-info payloads, marks final/proof roots only on clause roots, uses C-shaped root-backward display ordering with axiom-stack reversal and direct parent stack-pop ordering, and assigns display-only sequential ids with represented clause-parent, formula-parent, rewrite-demodulator, and signature AC axiom refs remapped for the printed list; for complete no-proof clause-list runs, it emits the C `Saturation` proof-object framing with represented processed roots plus reachable mixed ancestors, including PCL/TSTP derivation or source-info payloads, final/proof root markers only on roots, and display-only sequential ids/remapped parent refs. `--force-deriv=1/2` now enables represented stopped-outcome proof objects for supported incomplete/resource clause-list runs when a proof-output format is selected, uses C's `Derivation` status, expands represented list ancestors, adds unprocessed roots at level 2, supports `--proof-statistics` without list/graph output, and suppresses later saturated-state printing at level 2 like C. `--proof-graph` now emits represented mixed clause/formula GraphViz DOT graphs for supported proof-success and complete no-proof clause-list runs, using C-like sequential node ids to avoid archive-copy identifier collisions; graph modes above level 1 render C-shaped TSTP clause/formula labels plus represented derivations or source-info labels, proof-success DOT uses the same represented extraction roots and `--full-deriv` additions as list/statistics mode, and graph edges inherit the child node colour like C. `--proof-object=0` preserves C's accepted no-output surface when no earlier proof-output option enabled proof objects. Supported proof-success runs now mark represented clause ancestors, including signature AC axiom parents, before C-style GC analysis, so `--print-statistics --record-gcs` reports represented proof-search given-clause usage, and `--training-examples` prints the represented count/section/list output with C's positive/negative selector bits and selected LOP/TPTP/TSTP clause rendering. `--proof-statistics` now prints the C proof-object counter block for represented proof-success, complete saturation, and forced stopped roots whenever a proof object is enabled, including the no-list `--record-gcs`/`--force-deriv` cases and represented proof-success extraction roots plus `--full-deriv` roots. The marker, statistics traversal, graph traversal, and proof-object list traversal prefer selected archive copies for proof-step parents and original quote sources for `DCCnfQuote` parents when compact Rust references collide with original axioms, expand `DCACRes` signature AC axiom parents, resolve represented formula-parent refs from `f_axioms`, `f_ax_archive`, `definition_formula_archive`, and `f_archive`, and collapse structurally valid dummy quote copies even after literal mutation like C. ## Legacy Work Item

`--cpu-limit`, `--soft-cpu-limit`, and `--memory-limit` update the C-shaped hard, soft, schedule, memory, and derived heuristic-limit state. Supported proof-search runs now arm a cooperative CPU-clock deadline from the soft limit when present, otherwise the hard limit; soft deadline expiry returns the C-shaped user-resource outcome and `RESOURCE_OUT` exit status, while hard deadline expiry now returns through the hard CPU-limit finalizer with C's doubled-`COMCHAR` `ResourceOut` banner, stderr diagnostic, no-output-file direct-banner-before-buffered-stdout ordering, and `CPU_LIMIT_ERROR` exit status. Linux builds now expose C-shaped `getrlimit`/`setrlimit` soft/hard/full-limit wrappers, install the `SIGXCPU` handler in normal builds, apply C's initial `RLIMIT_CPU` choice (soft limit when present, otherwise hard limit), warn on reduced/failed CPU-limit setup with the C `SetSoftRlimitErr` message shapes including `strerror(errno)` text for unmasked failures, print C's separate `perror("eprover")` line before warning when core-dump suppression cannot be applied, capture the system hard CPU limit during signal setup, reset `RLIMIT_CPU` to that system limit on a soft timeout signal before rearming the hard limit, record the active configured-output descriptor for signal-time hard-timeout output, directly write C's hard-timeout banner/SZS and fatal stderr text from the normal hard `SIGXCPU` trampoline before exiting with `CPU_LIMIT_ERROR`, expose C's scheduler SIGTERM count-plus-default-reset handler shape, and apply the C `RLIMIT_DATA` memory behavior including the duplicated `RLIMIT_AS` branch bug that still passes `RLIMIT_DATA` and the failed-`RLIMIT_DATA` warning mask; native Windows keeps finite `--cpu-limit` on the cooperative process-CPU deadline because `JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_PROCESS_TIME` terminates with `STATUS_QUOTA_EXCEEDED` before C-shaped timeout output can be emitted, while nonzero `--memory-limit` still uses a retained Job Object process-memory limit when the current process can be assigned to one, warning on setup failures. Reference-verified signal delivery/output-file behavior and non-Linux hard-timeout shutdown remain tied to the platform shutdown abstraction. `--resources-info` writes the C preprocessing-time and footer shapes using `os_wrapper`; native Windows reports current-process user/system CPU time and peak working-set pages via `Kernel32`, and Linux now uses `getrusage(RUSAGE_SELF/RUSAGE_CHILDREN)` to sum user/system time while preserving C's parent-only raw `ru_maxrss` field under the historic "pages" label, with `/proc` fallback if the POSIX call fails. Exact maximum-resident-set unit matching remains target-dependent.

`TFormulaTSTPParse` parses formula-level `=` and `!=` as ordinary equality operators first, then rewrites them to equivalence and XOR when both operands have Boolean type while non-Boolean operands remain term equality. The C checks are type-based, not name-based, so an LFHOL user sort named `bool` is still an ordinary term sort; partial applications returning that sort, such as `col @ (lam @ A)`, must remain term-equality operands. Rust mirrors that behavior for supported compound formula operands, represented typed atomic-left Boolean equality/disequality, represented top-level, connective-operand, negated, and quantified-body atomic-left plus parenthesized compound-left formula equality/disequality, represented unparenthesized quantified-body equality/disequality, supported Boolean `$ite`/`$let` primary operands, top-level, connective-operand, negated, and quantified-body non-Boolean `$ite`/`$let` equality operands, non-Boolean `@` application equality RHS terms such as `c = (h @ a) @ b`, and non-`$o` partial-application equality such as `(col @ (lam @ A)) = A`; a full formula owner should keep the source spelling, semantic normalized connective, real `$o` versus user-sort distinction, and term-literal fallback as separate, explicit facts.

Separately, `TFormulaSetLiftItes` calls `do_ite_unroll` in the LFHO preprocessing branch, rewriting formula-position `$ite(C,T,F)` as `(~C|T)&(C|F)` and term-position `$ite` by replacing the nearest enclosing formula position without running Boolean equality replacement when `--fool-unroll` is disabled. Rust mirrors the term-level FOOL split behavior and stages the formula-set ITE owner path for direct formula-position Boolean `$ite`, first literal-side term-position `$ite`, and left-before-right scan order; parser-supported proof-search/CNF/prune `$ite` owners now route through represented formula owners with higher-order promotion so they reach that formula-set ITE path, while remaining bridge-only FOOL spellings still use the temporary executable lowering. ## Legacy Work Item

`ClauseSet` evaluation indices use safe sorted roots keyed by the C `EvalCompare` fields instead of storing the same raw `EvalCell*` nodes in per-position splay trees. Rust preserves best-clause ordering and root-clearing behavior. The first stable-slot prototype did not establish an end-to-end gain before shared-term weight caching, but the post-cache profile exposed 1.22-1.30 seconds of selection work across 4,897 clauses. The retained safe sparse store now resolves evaluation objects and removes clauses through private slots, tracks the first live slot for constant-time drains, and compacts only at safe insertion/batch boundaries; an adjacent rebuild A/B reduced median `LUSK6.lop` time from 6.54 to 5.79 seconds and selection to 0.085 seconds. These slots remain set-private until broader typed clause handles can replace cloned index/proof positions coherently.

title: Compatibility revisit #0229: SATCheck in C delegates to PicoSAT, applies its decision limit through the solver, exports either all clauses or the non-pure subset through the solver interface, and extracts PicoSAT's…
description:
## Source

- File: `docs/rust-port-status.md`

- Content SHA-256: `9fac5d094f928ba76852ab53cb5f68e9eb4d45f390b250bcc08cbfb9314dba41`

## Legacy Work Item

SATCheck in C delegates to PicoSAT, applies its decision limit through the solver, exports either all clauses or the non-pure subset through the solver interface, and extracts PicoSAT's unsat core into the generated empty clause. The extracted core is pushed in solver order but consumed with `PStackPopP`, so the generated empty-clause derivation records core parents in reverse stack order. Rust currently uses safe all/non-pure solver-clause export vectors plus an internal DPLL solver, deletion-minimizes the exported non-pure clause set after UNSAT, keeps exported-size statistics separate from minimized-core statistics, mirrors the reverse derivation-parent order, and records the represented SATCheck empty clause in the proof-state extraction-root stack. The SAT clause-set layer and proof-control SATCheck dispatch can also use the runtime-loaded PicoSAT wrapper, reset it to a fresh solver state around each exported SATCheck or fixed-limit core query, and map solver core positions back through the exported-subset stack when a caller, `E_RUST_PORT_PICOSAT_LIBRARY`, or bundled executable-relative library discovery installs a runtime solver; making PicoSAT mandatory/default for every SATCheck run still depends on packaging and the eager-allocation compatibility decision.

## Legacy Work Item

`SelectUnlessUniqMax`, `SelectUnlessPosMax`, `SelectUnlessUniqPosMax`, and `SelectUnlessUniqMaxPos` all depend on maximality marking. Rust keeps a bankless `DoLiteralSelection` helper for selectors that do not need the term bank and exposes `do_literal_selection_with_bank` for proof-control paths that own the live term bank. That banked wrapper now uses mutable-bank maximal marking for the table-visible ordering-dependent selector families, including largest/smallest-orientable, unless-maximal, complex unique-max Horn, MaxLComplex, base NewComplex, MinInfpos, AHP/VGNonCR, and CQ/UnlessPDom selectors. Full C selector-name coverage is present; the lower-level bankless helper only reports a diagnostic if a banked/ordering-dependent selector is reached without the required ordering/term-bank context, while legacy immutable selector helpers remain for compatibility callers outside proof-control. The `UniqPosMax` and `UniqMaxPos` variants intentionally differ when one positive maximal and another negative maximal literal coexist.

description:
## Source

- Content SHA-256: `ac2c6c6f9ca5ddfca9db5fd71a66d32952c5629631033e22d03a2adfd42bd823`

## Legacy Work Item

`--app-encode` is not just a passive encoding flag in C: it enables the app-encoded formula output path, writes to `stdout` even when `GlobalOut` is redirected, diverts bare includes through `ignore_include` by echoing them to stdout without loading the referenced files and rejecting selector syntax, expands `$distinct`, runs auto-mode preprocessing selection, SInE, and relevance pruning, then app-encodes the remaining formula set, skips top-level `$true` formulas, preserves source-level binary connective spellings in the printed formula path, parses clause owners before rendering only the formula set, and exits before pruning or proof search. Rust now preserves that print-and-exit shape for supported TPTP/TSTP formula entries by populating proof-state `f_axioms` and rendering them with `FormulaSetAppEncode`, including app-encode include echo/no-load behavior, generated auto preprocessing class/configuration output before the print-only branch, explicit `--print-types` suffixes on app-encoded term output, represented old-TPTP `input_formula(...)` app-encode owners that keep old-dialect formula equality/disequality as `=`/`!=`, represented non-`$distinct` TSTP `tff(...)`/`tcf(...)`/`thf(...)` and plain/application/typed-equality/unparenthesized-quantified-body-equality/bare-negated-left-equality/application-left-equality/applied-lambda FOF app-encode owners that share the staged `WFormula` app-encoding path, represented top-level `$distinct(...)` bodies expanded through proof-state `$distinct` processing before rendering, and represented formula-owner SInE/relevance pruning before rendering. Parsed-but-discarded non-watchlist `cnf(...)`/`input_clause(...)` entries may still affect shared-signature declarations and `--error-on-empty`, and watchlist-only app-encode input remains empty for `--error-on-empty` like C's `ProofStateAxNo` check. A later full implementation should decide whether the stdout-bypass, print-only auto classifier/scheduler work, clause-side declaration leakage, remaining FOF app-encode bridge shims, embedded `$distinct` bridge expansion, and spelling-preserving formula-rendering behavior should remain compatibility-only quirks.

## Legacy Work Item

Parser-supported formula-level Boolean `$ite`/`$let` owners, typed Boolean FOOL equality/disequality formulas, FOOL term arguments, and top-level/connective/negated/quantified non-Boolean FOOL equality/disequality operands now route through represented formula owners for print/syntax, app-encode, and proof/CNF paths, with proof/CNF inputs promoted to higher-order when FOOL terms remain so the represented `FormulaSetCNF2` route performs ITE/LET lifting. Remaining bridge-backed FOOL spellings still lower direct positive Boolean `$ite(C,T,F)` predicate literals through the C `do_ite_unroll` formula-position shape `(~C|T)&(C|F)`, and direct literals containing a term-position `$ite` lower the first occurrence on the left side before the right side into `(~C|L[T])&(C|L[F])`, matching C's direct literal-side scan for the supported bridge. Direct `$let` occurrences through supported quantifier/connective scopes lift before CNF by allocating fresh `epred`/`esk` definitions over captured and formal variables, replacing body occurrences, and clausifying Boolean definitions as equivalences or term definitions as equalities with free variables in generated definition clauses carrying the expected universal clause meaning; conjecture lowering keeps those generated definitions positive while negating only the rewritten conjecture body. App-encode and syntax-only printing still keep the original term encoding, while non-printing syntax-only exits before CNF lifting. The simple formula parser has a special primary-formula branch, reused by unparenthesized existential-body parsing, so equality and disequality around Boolean FOOL atoms are represented as equivalence and XOR instead of term equality, while non-Boolean `$ite`/`$let` primary terms remain valid only when immediately followed by `=` or `!=` and then lower as ordinary term literals. A full formula owner should model these as typed formula/term nodes, with explicit predicate-literal, `ite`/`let`, and term equality/disequality lowering steps instead of depending on predicate-position checks to recognize them.

Resource-limit APIs outside Linux and Windows still return explicit unsupported results. Keep future unsafe code similarly confined to external DLL/shared-library interop with documented invariants.
